text.title: Tree Testing Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a candidate hierarchy exists, whether browsing is a real access path in this product, and whether a rate-reporting sample is reachable — separating card sorting and first-click studies from a full quantitative tree test.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a complete candidate hierarchy — labels plus parent-child structure — ready to put under test?

branch.when: no hierarchy yet; labels and groupings are still being generated

conclusion.verdict: skip; run an open card sort first, then tree-test the hierarchy it produces

branch.question: How do people actually reach content in this product, and what is the question about?

branch.when: search, a feed or deep links carry the primary access path; browsing the hierarchy is a fallback few use

conclusion.verdict: skip; the navigation under test is not the path under load — test search relevance and result labelling instead

branch.when: the question is about page content, body copy wording or visual design rather than where an item lives

conclusion.verdict: skip; that is usability testing — a tree test strips visuals by design and cannot answer it

branch.when: browsing the hierarchy is a real access path and the question is where items live
branch.question: How many participants per tree variant can be recruited?

branch.when: fewer than about 30 per variant, or only one or two labels are genuinely in question

conclusion.verdict: run a first-click or label-comprehension study instead; if you still tree-test, report counts and observed paths rather than percentages and make no claim that one variant beat another

branch.when: around 50 per variant is reachable, but scenario wording still reuses words from the target label or its ancestors

conclusion.verdict: rewrite before launch; check each task against its full path and recast it as a situation rather than a request, otherwise the test measures word-matching

branch.when: around 50 per variant is reachable and task wording avoids the label vocabulary

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; text-only tree with no search or visuals, accepted destinations fixed before data collection, at most ten randomised tasks, success and directness reported as separate numbers
